anomaly: alarm on CNC-01: vibration 7.01 mm/s above 4.50
conclusion: CNC-01's vibration alarm (ticks 521-524, 7.01-7.37 mm/s) was a transient sensor/instrument disturbance, not a confirmed machine fault. Vibration spiked for exactly four ticks while spindle load (64.5-69.2%), temperature (122-126°F), power (~11.6-11.9 kW), and following error (3-5 µm) all stayed normal, then vibration returned to baseline ~2.2-2.4 mm/s at tick 525 and remained there through tick 530 with no recurrence. CNC-01 speed is unchanged at 1000 rpm. Alarms appear only on CNC-01; CNC-02 vibration was normal over the same window and the event log shows no other machine alarms. A real bearing fault would not self-recover in one tick with no load/temperature/power change, and benign job-8 variation does not explain a sustained 3x alarm-level spike isolated to one channel. Confidence ~0.80, below the 0.90 threshold for an intervene; moreover none of the available human-approved actions (replace_bearing, reset_setting, replace_servo_drive, repair_hydraulics) addresses a vibration-sensor transient, so no change is indicated. Monitor CNC-01 and inspect the vibration sensor if similar spikes recur; an inspection report confirming sensor health would raise confidence further.

anomaly: alarm on CNC-03: vibration 5.12 mm/s above 4.50
conclusion: CNC-03's vibration alarm (ticks 71-78, about 5.0-5.21 mm/s against a 4.50 mm/s threshold) is a spurious sensor/channel reading, not a mechanical fault. CNC-03 was idle for the whole window (load near 0 percent, E9), its following error stayed small (mean 0.84 µm, E12), and vibration fell back to normal (~0.175 mm/s at tick 80) immediately after the alarm ended (E11). A real mechanical defect would not appear and vanish within seconds while the machine is doing no work. All other checked machines are normal: CNC-01 and CNC-02 run at ~2-2.6 mm/s (E7, E8), and CNC-04/CNC-05 are under 0.4 mm/s during the same ticks (E13, E14). CNC-03 itself lists no hydraulics (E3). Most likely cause: a faulty vibration sensor or its wiring channel on CNC-03 (H1). None of the human-approvable changes (bearing, setting reset, servo drive, hydraulics) repairs a vibration sensor, and stopping a healthy machine would not fix anything.
